subject: math

objective.text: Use a ruler as a number line to show sums and differences about length.

explanations.title: More length means add
explanations.text: To show 20 more than 35, start at 35. Slide right 20. Count by fives or tens. Where you stop is the answer. 35 plus 20 equals 55.

explanations.title: Less length means subtract
explanations.text: To show 15 less than 55, start at 55. Slide left 15. Where you stop is the answer. 55 minus 15 equals 40.

explanations.title: Length of an object
explanations.text: Put one end of the object at one endpoint. The length is the distance from the left end to the right end. Count the units, or subtract the two endpoints.

explanations.title: Slide the object to make it easier
explanations.text: Sliding an object does not change its length. Slide it so one end is on a ten. 62 minus 49 is the same as 63 minus 50. Both equal 13.

explanations.title: Count jumps, not marks
explanations.text: Know how long each unit is. Skip-count by that length. Count the jumps, not the hash marks.

explanations.title: Make a hundred to add
explanations.text: To add 420 and 190, take 10 from 420. Give it to 190 to make 200. Then add 410 and 200.

examples.title: 20 more than 35
examples.text: Start at 35. Slide right 20. Each unit is 5. You stop at 55. 35 plus 20 equals 55.

examples.title: 15 less than 55
examples.text: Start at 55. Slide left 15. You stop at 40. 55 minus 15 equals 40.

examples.title: Length of the pencil
examples.text: A pencil goes from 49 to 62. 62 minus 49 equals 13. Slide it 1 unit right. Now it goes from 50 to 63. 63 minus 50 equals 13. The pencil is 13 units long.
